title: Count of restrictions with a fixed number of free variables
statement: Fix natural numbers $n$ and $k$. Among all restrictions on $n$ variables — maps assigning each index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ either a fixed Boolean value or leaving it free — the number of those having exactly $k$ free variables equals $\binom{n}{k}\,2^{\,n-k}$.
hypotheses_covered: k : natural number, the prescribed count of free variables
replaced:
The number of restrictions of $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ with exactly $k$ free variables
equals $\binom{n}{k} \cdot 2^{\,n-k}$.
